info.title: AmoBot API
info.description:
Everything AmoBot answers over HTTP, as JSON (the panels are static files and render their own pages). Two panels,
each with its API and its session: `/api/admin/*` is the owner's (signed in with the login config.php keeps, each
request worked in the shop it names — `X-Shop`, the shop its tab shows —: the session remembers no shop),
`/api/agent/*` an agent's (signed in with the main bot's one-time link, in their bot's shop). The shop's own screens
are the same in both: they are described once, under `/api/{panel}/…`; what only one panel has is under its own
prefix. Every panel request carries the session cookie, and one that changes something also sends
`X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` (the CSRF guard). `/api/app` is public; `/api/install/*` answers only
until the shop is installed, and only to a request carrying the install key (`X-Install-Key`: the text of
storage/install-key.txt, which the first request makes — without it, a 403 that says so on `key`). Every answer
names its request in `X-Request-Id` — an error answer in its body too (`request_id`) —, and every log line the
request wrote carries the same id.

`/api/store/v1/{store}/*` is the Store API — a shop's own website, the main bot's or an agent's: the website's store
key names the shop, a customer signs in (Telegram, Google, an email and a password — and its second step, when the
account asks one) for a bearer token of their own (the `customer` scheme: no cookie, no session, no CSRF header),
and a page on the website's origins may call it from a browser (CORS: a preflight is answered, and every answer — an
error's too — says the origin may read it). What the shop sells — its plans as its bot offers them now, and how the
servers they are sold on stand — is anyone's to read, and so are the customers' reviews support approved, with their
count and average rating, while the website shows them; anyone may write one then — a guest behind the website's
captcha, while it asks none a signed-in customer alone —, waiting on support until it is approved — a signed-in
customer's bearer token with it makes it theirs. Signed in, a customer keeps
their own account: their names, their password, two-factor sign-in, the ways in — added (a way in another account of
the shop has is a merge offered, 202) and taken away —, the devices signed in; what changes how the account is
signed in to (the password, two-factor sign-in, a way in, a merge) asks a sign-in of the last 15 minutes too, else a
403 whose `WWW-Authenticate` says so — POST /me/reauthenticate proves a way in again, so a bearer token alone changes
none of it. They read what is theirs alone: their services (one read from its panel now, its automatic renewal
switched, its link changed), their orders and payments, their wallet and its ledger, their part in the referral
program, and every notice the shop told them (read or not); they order through the bot's own checkout — a plan, a
service's renewal, a wallet top-up, each request with its `Idempotency-Key` — and upload a card transfer's receipt;
and they talk to support in tickets — opened about a service or none, written to with a picture or without, closed,
opened again by a message, rated —, support answering from the shop's panels or its report group. A form of the
site's own (a contact form) may ask the website's captcha too: the site's backend has the shop judge the widget's
token (POST /captcha/verify), so the site never holds its secret. A body the Store API takes is JSON (`Content-Type:
application/json`) — a form only where a picture may come with it (a receipt, a ticket's message) —: any other is a
415.

`/api/store/v1/{store}/admin/*` is the shop's daily work again — the panels' own operations, each one this file
marks `x-staff` (its value the grant the shop must give for it, `true` for none) —, for the shop's admins (its
customers whose role is admin) signed in on its website with their bearer token: it answers while the website lets
them in (`staff_enabled`); a session signed in with a password alone is refused while the website asks a strong
sign-in (`staff_strong_sign_in`: Telegram, Google, or a password with its second step — POST /me/reauthenticate
proves one); every operation asks a way in proven on the session within the last 12 hours — an admin's token works
for a working day, not for the months a customer's lasts —; an operation that names a grant answers while the website
grants it (`staff_grants`) and asks a recent sign-in too (the last 15 minutes), as approving a payment, which
delivers a service, does (`x-staff-recent`). Each refusal is a 403 (`StaffRefused`); the shop's configuration —
its payment methods, the bot's settings, texts and keyboards, its report group, its website, who its admins are — is
no admin's on the website (a 404). An admin decides nothing about themselves (their own payment approved or given
back, their own wallet, their own service changed — days and traffic, switched off or on, moved, deleted —, their own
review approved, rejected or deleted), touches no admin's account nor an agent's, approves no payment without a
receipt in review, and leaves no client on a panel that answers — guards of an admin's own account alone: two admins
may do for each other what each is refused for themselves, so a shop lets in only people it trusts. The admins'
paths are the panels' paths, described once: tests/Support/ApiDescription expands each marked operation to its
`/admin` path — the store key in place of the panel, the `customer` bearer scheme, the 401 and the 403.

The Store API is versioned in its address: this is v1. Within v1 an answer only gains fields — none is removed,
renamed or given another type, and a request takes what it took —, so a website keeps working across the shop's
upgrades; a change that would break one comes as v2, beside v1. Every refusal and failure is the one error shape, its
`message` in the reader's words — the customer's on the Store API, the admin's on the panels.

This file is the contract both sides are checked against: every request the PHP tests send and every response they
get back must match it (tests/HttpTestCase), every route must be in it and nothing else, every POST, PUT and PATCH
describes its body or says it takes none (`x-no-body: true`) (tests/Unit/Http/ApiDescriptionTest), and the panels'
types are generated from it (`pnpm api:types` writes resources/panel/src/lib/api-types.ts). Objects are closed: a
field the server sends, or a request carries, that is not described here fails the tests.

post.summary: A nonce for an id_token sign-in (Telegram's popup, Google) — a sign-in's, or a signed-in customer's adding or proving a way in: the site opens the provider's sign-in with it, and posts it back with the token — once. 429 once this address network asked for 120 nonces, states and codes in 10 minutes (one address is many customers on a mobile network); 503 while the shop keeps as many sign-ins begun as it takes (5000 nonces in their half hour).

Telegram's sign-in by redirect, begun in this browser: where to send it — the site makes the PKCE verifier and keeps it, sending the challenge; the state (keeping the challenge) and the nonce are the shop's — the state a sign-in's: POST /auth/telegram alone takes it back, with the verifier (a signed-in customer's own is POST /me/telegram/authorize's). 422 while the website keeps no client secret, or on `redirect_uri` or `code_challenge`; 429 once this address network asked for 120 nonces, states and codes in 10 minutes; 503 while the shop keeps as many sign-ins begun as it takes.

Sign in with Telegram — the popup's id_token, or the redirect's code with the state POST /auth/telegram/authorize gave and the verifier of the challenge it was given (a signed-in customer's state, or a code and state brought back to another browser, signs nobody in): the shop's customer with that Telegram account, or a newcomer made as the bot makes one. 401 when it does not sign anyone in, 403 banned, 422 Telegram sign-in off or a field missing, 429 too many failures from this address network (30 in 15 minutes), 502 Telegram out of reach.

200.description: Signed in — the bearer token, shown this once

post.summary: Sign in with Google — the id_token Google Identity Services handed the page, with the nonce it was asked for: the shop's customer with that Google account, else the one with the address Google speaks for (which signs in with Google from then on, its customer told), else a newcomer. The address counts only where Google is its own authority — `email_verified`, and an @gmail.com address or a Google Workspace account's (`hd`); any other address finds, takes on and keeps no account. 401 when it does not sign anyone in, 403 banned, 409 the address is an account's that takes no Google account on by it — one with two-factor sign-in on, or another Google account's: signed in its own way, the customer adds Google from their account —, 422 Google sign-in off, 429 too many failures from this address network, 502 Google out of reach.

200.description: Signed in — the bearer token, shown this once

post.summary: Sign up with an email: a six-digit code to the address (POST /auth/register/verify takes it back) — or, when the address has an account, an email saying so; the answer is the same either way. Again: a new code in the last one's place. 422 email sign-up off, or a field (the captcha's too), 429 a code went to the address a minute ago, the address had its ten emails today (from every shop), this address network its twenty an hour (or asked too much), or the codes sent to the address were failed until it waits (ten wrong an hour, twenty a day); 502 the email did not go; 503 the shop's email does not go out, or the shop's (or every shop's) budget of emails is spent — sixty an hour, three hundred a day a shop —, or the captcha could not be judged.

202.description: Emailed — a code, or that the address has an account

post.summary: Finish signing up with the code the email carried: the account made — reported, its invite code's owner told — and signed in. 409 the address took an account meanwhile, 422 the code is wrong, expired, spent or tried five times (or email sign-up off), 429 too many failures — or the address's budget of wrong codes spent: ten an hour, twenty a day, each counted before it is checked, whatever codes were sent.

200.description: Signed up and in — the bearer token, shown this once

post.summary: Sign in with an email and its password — an account with two-factor sign-in on answers its second step's challenge instead (202; POST /auth/login/2fa finishes it). 401 for either wrong (one answer: which addresses have an account is told nobody), 403 banned, 422 a field (the captcha's too), 429 too many failures from this address network (30 in 15 minutes) or for this account (50, from every address), 503 the captcha could not be judged.

200.description: Signed in — the bearer token, shown this once

202.description: The password was right; the account asks the code of its authenticator app — no session yet

post.summary: A password sign-in's second step: the challenge it answered, with the six-digit code of the account's authenticator app (Persian digits too; a code opens once) or one of its recovery codes (spent). A reset's new password the challenge keeps is set now, every other session of the account ended. 401 the challenge opens nothing any more (expired, five wrong codes, two-factor turned off since — sign in again), 403 banned, 422 a field missing or the code wrong, 429 too many failures from this address network or for this account — or the account's second-step codes spent: 10 an hour and 20 a day, counted before each is checked, whoever tries them (the customer is told once a day).

200.description: Signed in — the bearer token, shown this once

post.summary: A forgotten password: a six-digit code to the address when it has an account — and to one without, an email saying it has none, once a day (asked again that day, nothing goes); the answer the same either way. 422 the address or the captcha, 429 a code went to the address a minute ago, the address had its ten emails today (from every shop), this address network its twenty an hour (or asked too much), or the codes sent to the address were failed until it waits (ten wrong an hour, twenty a day); 502 the email did not go; 503 the shop's email does not go out, or the shop's (or every shop's) budget of emails is spent, or the captcha could not be judged.

202.description: Taken — a code is on its way when the address has an account

post.summary: A new password with the code POST /auth/password/forgot emailed: kept, every session of the account ended, this device signed in, the customer told — or, two-factor sign-in on (a reset leaves it on), its second step's challenge (202), nothing changed yet: the new password waits in it, and POST /auth/login/2fa sets it. 403 banned, 422 a field — the code wrong, expired, spent or tried five times —, 429 too many failures — or the address's budget of wrong codes spent: ten an hour, twenty a day, each counted before it is checked (its account told once a day).

200.description: Set, and signed in — the bearer token, shown this once

customer.description: A website's customer: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, the token their sign-in answered (64 hex characters) — one per device. A session ends — every request with its token a 401 from then on, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`: sign in again — when the customer signs that device out (POST /auth/logout) or ends it from another (DELETE /me/sessions/{id}); when their password is changed (PUT /me/password, or set by a merge: every session but the one that changed it) or reset (POST /auth/password/reset, or its second step: every session); when support signs them out of every device from a panel; when a twenty-first session opens (the oldest ends — twenty a customer at most); after 30 days unused; and 180 days after its sign-in. A banned customer's token is a 403. What changes how the account is signed in to asks the token's sign-in to be recent too — within 15 minutes, or a way in proven again since (POST /me/reauthenticate) —, else a 403 whose `WWW-Authenticate` says so (`Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", max_age=900`).

Shop.name: X-Shop
Shop.description: The shop the request is worked in, by its bot's id (ShopRef.id; 1 is the main bot's): every request of the owner's panel names the shop its tab shows — the tab's address says it (`/admin/s/7/…`; `/admin/…` the main bot's) —, so the session remembers no shop and two tabs work in a shop each. None named is the main bot's shop; one that is no bot's id is a 422 on `shop`, a bot that is not there a 404 on `shop` (never the main shop in its place) — the sign-in's too, once its credentials are found right. A sign-in answers the session in the shop named. The owner's sections that are the shop's as a whole work where they belong whatever is named (the servers across every bot's services, the agency and the panel's settings in the main bot's shop). An agent's panel names none — their shop is their bot: naming another bot is a 403 on `shop`.

ShopQuery.name: shop
ShopQuery.description: The shop, as `X-Shop` names it, for what a picture, a video or a download link asks for — no header goes with those (the panel adds it to every such address). A read alone may name it here; a change names it in the header (a 422 on `shop` otherwise), and a header and a query that name two shops are a 422 too.

TextKey.name: key

Search.name: search

Status.description: The status tab; empty for all

Dir.name: dir

To.description: The last day of the list (a date of the shop's calendar, included); anything else is no end

Store.name: store

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A key the website makes for each checkout attempt (a UUID) — a new one when the customer picks another way to pay: 1 to 64 Latin letters, digits, `-` and `_`. The same request made again with it — a network's retry, the same `method_id` — is answered by the order it came to — the one it made, or the open one of the same thing it found and paid —, as it stands: never a second order or a second charge, whatever changed since (a price included: the order is the one made at the price then); two made in the same moment get one order and one answer. One whose order was cancelled since — by support, or left unpaid past its time, maybe days ago — is a 409 in words of its own («این سفارش لغو شده است…»; not the 409 of an order closed elsewhere a moment ago): buying it again is a new attempt, with a new key. A key that came to an order of something else (another type, plan, server or service — a top-up of another amount), or was first sent with another `method_id` (the order would be paid another way), is a 422 on `idempotency_key`, and so is none, or a malformed one. A key answers for its order a week; after that a request with it is a new one.

Error.description: Refused or failed, in the one error shape

SignedOut.description: The bearer token opens no session of the shop's — none sent, one that ended (the `customer` scheme says what ends one), another shop's — «برای دسترسی باید وارد شوید.»: the customer signs in again. Never a refusal of what the request asked (that is a 4xx of its own: a proof that does not hold is a 422 on its field), so a website may take any 401 here as signed out.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer` (RFC 6750): what the operation asks for is a bearer token.

SignInAgain.description: This session's sign-in is not recent enough to change how the account is signed in to — «برای این کار دوباره وارد شوید.»: a way into the account proven again (POST /me/reauthenticate) opens it for 15 minutes. (A banned customer's 403 says so in its message, without the header.)

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", max_age=900` (RFC 9470): a sign-in at most this many seconds old.

StaffRefused.description: One of the shop's admins on its website refused at its admin API's door, or a decision no admin makes there: a customer who is no admin of the shop (whatever the website says) — «این بخش فقط برای پشتیبانی فروشگاه است.»; one while the website lets no admin in; a session signed in with a password alone while the website asks a strong sign-in (its `WWW-Authenticate` names the strong ways — POST /me/reauthenticate proves one); a session whose sign-in is older than 12 hours, whatever the operation (SignInAgain's challenge); an operation the website has not granted its admins; a granted operation, or a payment's approval, whose session's sign-in is older than 15 minutes (SignInAgain's challenge); a decision about themselves — their own payment approved or given back, their own wallet, their own service changed (days and traffic, switched off or on, moved, deleted) —, an admin's account or an agent's, a payment approved without a receipt in review; a banned customer.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", acr_values="telegram google password_2fa"` (RFC 9470) for a sign-in too weak, `Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", max_age=900` for one not recent enough; none otherwise.

Receipt.description: A receipt's bytes: a picture the panel shows (inline), or — any other type — a file to save (attachment)

TicketPicture.description: A ticket message's picture, as its bytes: a picture shown as itself, or — any other type — a file to save (attachment)

ErrorResponse.description: Every refusal and failure — a controller's, a middleware's, the error handler's, the front controller's last resort. A 429 says its wait in `Retry-After` (seconds) too.

message.description: In the reader's words: the admin's on the panels, the customer's on the Store API.

errors.description: What to fix, under the field it is about

request_id.description: The request's id, as its `X-Request-Id` header says it and every log line of it carries it — what the panel shows on a failure of the server's own («کد پیگیری»), to find the request in the log.

debug.description: Only for a failure of the server's (a 500, never a refusal), with APP_DEBUG on, and only to a request straight from the server's own machine — never one a proxy or a tunnel forwarded. Paths are told from the app's folder; no call's arguments.

PageMeta.description: Where a paged list is. A sorted list's meta says its order beside these (`sort`, `dir`).

SortDirection.description: Which way a sorted list runs — asc (the oldest, the smallest, the soonest first) or desc.

UserRef.description: The customer as every screen points at them — the three Telegram identifiers, kept apart (a customer who signed up on the website has none but a name), their email, plus our id.

name.description: "first last" as Telegram has it, or as they signed up with; null when the account shows none.

username.description: Bare Telegram handle without "@"; null when the account has none.

telegram_id.description: Their Telegram account; null for one who signed up on the website — the bot cannot write to them.

email.description: Their email (lower case, proven); null while they have none.

WholeNumberInput.description: A whole number as a form sends it: a JSON number, or its text — Persian or Arabic digits too.

AmountInput.description: An amount as a form sends it: a JSON number, or its text — Persian or Arabic digits and thousands separators too. Toman are whole (the form this API answers them in, "120000.00" — a fraction of zero —, is taken; any other fraction is refused); gigabytes may have up to two decimals.

NumbersInput.description: A short list of whole numbers — the amounts a screen offers as buttons —: a list, or the text an admin types ("50, 100, 200", or a space between; a comma between groups of three digits sets a number's thousands apart: "50,000, 100,000" is two numbers); kept without repeats, smallest first.

NoteRequest.description: Support's word to the customer that comes with a decision — a cancel, a rejection, a service switched off, an agency refused or ended: its own line of the message they get; 300 characters at most, blank for none.

RefundRequest.description: Support's word on a refund: its own line of the message the customer gets, and the note of the wallet line the refund writes — 190 characters at most, a ledger line's (Ledger::NOTE_MAX); blank for none.

ReorderRequest.description: An admin-ordered list's rows in their new order, by id — 1000 at most (Sorting::MAX_IDS), as many as a list may have.

ActivationRequest.description: The on/off switch of a row in its list (a plan, a category): true or false, nothing else.

database.description: Never why: the log has that.

name.description: The shop's name (APP_NAME), as the brand shows it.

installed.description: False until the web installer has finished: the panel then opens it.

timezone.description: The shop's time zone (APP_TIMEZONE, an IANA name such as Asia/Tehran): the panels show every date and time in it, as the bot words its dates.

FieldType.description: What a field holds, as a generic form draws it: a line of text, a whole number, an amount of Toman, a short list of numbers typed as text, an on/off switch, one of a few values, a secret, an email address, a web address, a file's path, a few lines of text, or a bank card's number (drawn in groups of four, as it is printed, and sent as its digits).

FieldDescription.description: One field of a driver's form as a generic form draws it (Field::describe()): the screens hold no driver's code.

name.description: The key it is sent under, and the one a 422 names.

required.description: A form that leaves it empty is refused — a secret's: one must end up kept, the stored one staying while it is left blank.

secret.description: Never sent back — its value is a SecretState —: left blank or left out it keeps the stored one, `clear_<name>: true` empties it.

bound_to.description: A secret's: the fields it belongs with. While one of them moves a blank one is refused (in `moved`'s words), to be typed again or cleared.

moved.description: What the server says of a blank secret while a field it belongs with moved — the hint to show before it is asked.

options.description: A choice's values and their words, in order.

when.description: Shown — and read, and required when it is — only while each named field (one before it) holds one of these values: a switch as "true" or "false", a number as its digits. Hidden, what is kept of it stays.

min.description: The least a number may be — each of a list's, an amount's.

ltr.description: Latin content (a host, a username): drawn left to right, as a number, a secret, an email, a web address and a path are.

default.description: What it holds while nothing is kept; null for a secret.

DriverDescription.description: A driver — one way of doing a thing through someone else: a database, a way email goes out — as the panels show it (Descriptor::toArray()): its name and words, and its form, every field described.

key.description: What config.php, a row or a request names it by.

notes.description: Short lines under the description: the versions it needs, its caveats.

traits.description: What its family says of it beyond this: a database driver's `installable` (the installer offers it); a mail driver's `sender` (who it can send from, in words); a payment gateway's `kind` (instant — it settles at once, the wallet —, or manual — a card transfer whose receipt a person accepts) and `builtin` (part of the shop itself: never added nor deleted); a panel connector's `mark` (the two letters its card draws), `vendor`, `docs` (its project's address) and what its panel can do — `inbounds` (services sold on inbounds the owner picks; without, a server is sold whole) and `link_rotation` («تغییر لینک»). A captcha driver has none.

DriverValues.description: A driver's fields by name as a screen shows them (Form::present()): as config.php holds them, else their defaults — a secret as its SecretState, never the secret.

DatabaseSettings.description: The database part of config.php: the driver DB_CONNECTION names, the drivers the admin may pick — each described, its form —, and the driver's fields as config.php holds them.

drivers.description: The installable drivers, and the one the shop runs on

DatabaseRequest.description: The database part of config.php as a form sends it — the installer's step, the settings screen's save and its test: the driver (one of `drivers`) and its form's fields under their names, as typed. A secret left blank or left out keeps the stored one while the address it was given for stays — in the installer there is none: it is empty —, and `clear_<name>: true` empties it. A closed shape per driver.

DatabaseMysqlRequest.description: MySQL or MariaDB: where the database is, the account on it, its tables' prefix.

password.description: Left out or blank: the one kept stays — while the host, the port and the socket stay.

clear_password.description: True: the kept password is emptied.

DatabaseSqliteRequest.description: SQLite: a file of the shop's own.

path.description: The file, relative to the application or absolute; never under public/.

InstallStatus.description: GET /api/install, and every installer step's answer — where the installation stands.

optional.description: What the shop runs without — the owner's panel updating it itself needs it: shown, and holding nothing up.

ready.description: Every requirement that is not optional is met.

database.description: The database step's settings, and whether a database answers to what config.php names (not asked before the step wrote one).

drivers.description: The installable drivers, and the one the shop runs on

tables.description: Every table of database/schema.php is there.

error.description: Why it does not answer, in the admin's words

InstallAdminRequest.description: The panel's login by its one rule (Auth's Credentials): a username of 2 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `@` or `-`, and a password of 8 characters at least and 72 bytes at most, typed twice alike.

password.description: As typed — a space at either end is part of it.

InstallSiteRequest.description: The shop's name and the address it is reached at (APP_NAME, APP_URL), and the main bot's token when the owner has it now — written once Telegram says whose it is.

token.description: From @BotFather; blank or left out — later, from the settings screen.

Session.description: Who is signed in to a panel and the shop the request was worked in: on the owner's panel the one login config.php keeps and the shop the request named (X-Shop), on an agent's their bot and its shop.

name.description: The owner's login, or the agent's bot (@username) — what their decisions are recorded under.

shops.description: Every shop the owner may open — the main bot's first.

ShopRef.description: A bot's shop: the main bot's, or an agent's.

id.description: The bot's id — 1 is the main bot.

name.description: The main bot's «فروشگاه اصلی»; an agent's bot's title, else — not handed over yet — «نماینده: » and the agent's name.

status.description: disabled: an agent whose agency ended — the shop is kept, its bot does not run.

password.description: As typed — a space at either end is part of it.

CredentialsRequest.description: The owner changes the panel's login: their current password first, then the new login by the installer's rule (InstallAdminRequest) — a password left blank, its confirmation too, keeps the one kept; a change that changes nothing is refused.

password.description: As typed — a space at either end is part of it.

RecoveryRequest.description: A new panel login set without the old one: the key the panel wrote to the host's files (RecoveryKeyResponse.file), then the login by the installer's rule (InstallAdminRequest).

key.description: As the file holds it; case and the spaces around it do not matter.

password.description: As typed — a space at either end is part of it.

file.description: Where the key is, from the shop's own folder: storage/recovery-key.txt.

expires_at.description: When it stops opening anything — an hour after it was made.

AgentLinkRequest.description: The code of the one-time link the main bot gave the agent («ورود به پنل»), read off the address's fragment (`#code=`).

replace.description: Sign in even though another agent's session is open in this browser — it ends. Left out: refused with a 409 on `replace`, the link not spent.

ChangesResponse.description: Each area's number (Core\Database\ChangeFeed::AREAS); an area nothing was written to yet is absent.

users.description: The customers, their wallets and their groups.

grants.description: The grants and their parts on each server — a running one's cursor moves every second.

plans.description: The plans, their categories and their server entries.

agency.description: The agency's levels and requests, the agents' bots and their traffic.

channels.description: The channels a customer must join.

reports.description: The report group, its topics and its queue.

emoji.description: The premium emoji the bot has seen.

tickets.description: The support tickets and their messages.

reviews.description: The customers' reviews of the shop.

ClientErrorRequest.description: A failure of the panel's own code, as its page reports it (ClientErrors): one error line of the shop's log with the shop's version, never kept anywhere else. Each part is cut to its length and taken out of any secret, the body is refused past 16 KB (413), and a principal or an address sends 20 in ten minutes and 100 in a day (429, `Retry-After`).

kind.description: `render` a page it could not draw (an error boundary, the router's error screen); `unhandled` an error a press or a promise left unhandled.

message.description: What was thrown: the error's name and its message.

stack.description: The top of the error's stack.

component_stack.description: Where in the page's components it was drawing (a render failure's).

address.description: The panel's address it happened at — its path and query, never the fragment (a sign-in link's code).

build.description: The panel build the page runs: when `vite build` made it.

QueueCounts.description: How many wait on a human in the shop — the sidebar's numbers, the first rows of the dashboard's attention card.

stuck_orders.description: Orders paid and not delivered: the delivery failed, or nobody is delivering it (the orders list's stuck tab).

open_tickets.description: Support tickets waiting on an answer (the tickets list's open tab).

pending_reviews.description: Customers' reviews waiting on support (the reviews list's pending tab).

UserRole.description: admin = the shop's people inside the bot — /broadcast, exempt from the bot's rules — and on its website (its admin API, while the website lets them in). Not the panel login.

UserRow.description: One row of the users table: a customer of the bot (the panel's own login is not one).

name.description: "first last" as Telegram has it, or as they signed up with; null when the account shows none.

username.description: Bare Telegram handle without "@"; null when the account has none.

telegram_id.description: Their Telegram account; null for one who signed up on the website — the bot cannot write to them.

email.description: Their email (lower case, proven); null while they have none.

phone.description: E.164, once shared with the bot.

groups.description: The admin's groups the customer is in, in the admin's order.

UserSort.description: What the users table sorts by: when each joined (the list's own order), was last seen, the balance (no ledger is 0), the orders, the running services.

UserDetailResponse.description: GET /users/{id} — one customer, as their page shows them; their services, orders and payments are those lists' own, narrowed to them (`user=`).

agency.description: The customer as an agent of the main bot, as the agents list shows them — their level and credit, their bot and what it sold; null for anyone who is not one (so in every agent's shop).

CustomerAccount.description: The customer's account on the shop's website, as support reads it: its ways in, whether its password sign-in asks a second step, the devices signed in, and the accounts merged into it.

email.description: Their email — proven; null without one.

google.description: A Google account signs them in.

has_password.description: Their email and a password sign them in.

two_factor.description: Their password sign-in asks the code of their authenticator app.

sessions.description: The devices signed in on the website — the sessions that have not ended.

merges.description: The accounts merged into this one, newest first.

CustomerMerge.description: An account of the shop merged into this customer's — its row gone since —: how it was signed in and called, and when the customer merged them (from their website: the one way two accounts are made one).

merged_user_id.description: Its former number in the shop.

telegram_id.description: The Telegram account it had; null for none.

google.description: A Google account signed it in.

name.description: "first last", as it was; null without one.

UserRoleRequest.description: Make a customer the bot's admin, or take it back.

UserGroupsRequest.description: The admin's groups the customer is in: every one listed, no other — an empty list takes them out of all.

CustomerReferral.description: The referral program's facts about a customer: whose link brought them, how many their own link brought and what those earned them.

referrer.description: The customer whose link brought them; null when none did.

earned.description: What the commissions credited to them add up to, in Toman — each kept as theirs when it was earned, two accounts merged since or not.

CustomerGroupRef.description: One of the admin's groups of customers, as a customer's row carries it.

CustomerGroupRow.description: One of the admin's groups of customers («گروه»): a name, in the admin's order; a broadcast can go to one.

name.description: Unique in the shop.

WalletTransactionRow.description: One line of a customer's wallet ledger.

reviewer.description: Who wrote it by hand — a panel's principal, or one of the shop's admins on its website — as its reader may see it (anyone but the owner reads the owner's login as «پشتیبانی»); null for the lines the shop writes itself.

WalletAdjustmentRequest.description: A credit or a debit by hand — a debit no further than the balance —, with the line the customer reads in their ledger.

description.description: The ledger line, 190 characters at most; blank for support's default wording.

revenue.description: Money that came in (Toman): paid payments not made from the wallet, and refunded ones but a wallet top-up's.

stuck_orders.description: Orders paid and not delivered: the delivery failed, or nobody is delivering it (the orders list's stuck tab).

open_tickets.description: Support tickets waiting on an answer (the tickets list's open tab).

pending_reviews.description: Customers' reviews waiting on support (the reviews list's pending tab).

servers_with_errors.description: The shop's servers whose panel failed its last read — 0 in an agent's shop.

traffic_shortage.description: An agent's shop whose traffic sells nothing; null while it sells, and in the main bot's shop.

expiring_days.description: The one "ending soon" window, in days — the subscriptions screen's too.

name.description: "first last" as Telegram has it, or as they signed up with; null when the account shows none.

username.description: Bare Telegram handle without "@"; null when the account has none.

telegram_id.description: Their Telegram account; null for one who signed up on the website — the bot cannot write to them.

email.description: Their email (lower case, proven); null while they have none.

BotRuntime.description: How a bot runs. The main bot's is the installation's: every bot gets its updates its way (on webhooks, or polling — they are put on webhooks and taken off together), and its token is config.php's.

configured.description: It has a token to run on.

enabled.description: Its shop's master switch (تنظیمات ربات), independent of whether the process is running.

username.description: Its @username, without the @; null while unknown.

BotMode.description: How a bot gets its updates: a webhook Telegram calls, a poller (bot:poll) whose heartbeat is fresh, or none of them.

SystemStatus.description: Whether the machinery behind the shop is alive — the owner's alone.

bot.description: The bot of the shop the request names (the dashboard's): the main bot, or an agent's.

configured.description: It has a token to run on.

enabled.description: Its shop's master switch (تنظیمات ربات), independent of whether the process is running.

username.description: Its @username, without the @; null while unknown.

WebhookOutcome.description: What putting the bots on webhooks, or taking them off, did for one of them — in the owner's words, never a token nor the secret a webhook's address ends with.

id.description: The bot's id — 1 is the main bot.

username.description: Its @username, without the @; null while unknown.

message.description: What happened, or why it did not.

bots.description: Every bot the shop runs, the main one first; none while no bot has a token.

UpdateStatus.description: AmoBot's own update: the version the shop runs, the newest release GitHub publishes, and the update under way or the last one. The shop installs only a release the key built into it signed.

latest.description: The newest release, as last read; null while GitHub publishes none, or before it was first read.

checked_at.description: When GitHub was last read; null before it ever was.

available.description: The newest release is newer than the version the shop runs, and no update is under way — nor has just installed it.

blocker.description: What keeps the shop from updating itself — no release key to check a release with, PHP without its sodium or zip extension, PHP that may not change the app's files, a release without its signed files — in the owner's words, with the way out (an update by hand: docs/Upgrading.md); null when nothing does.

run.description: The update under way, or the last one; null when there is none.

ReleaseInfo.description: A release as GitHub lists it.

version.description: Its version (its tag, without the v).

notes.description: Its notes, as plain text: shown as they are, line breaks kept — never as HTML.

UpdateStep.description: Where an update stands: its files fetched and checked (download), unpacked (extract), the host checked (preflight), installed (install) — then done, or taken back once installed (rolled_back). from.description: The version the shop ran when it began — the one a rollback puts back.

progress.description: How far into its step, in percent.

error.description: Why its step was last refused, in the owner's words; null while nothing stands in its way.

cancel.description: It may still be given up: nothing of the app's was replaced yet.

rollback.description: It may be taken back: installed, the version it replaced kept, and the database not changed by it.

finished_at.description: When it was installed or taken back; null while under way.

version.description: The newest release — `latest.version`: an update is to it, and nothing else.

GatewayKind.description: How a gateway settles: at once (the wallet), or once a person — or the method's review window — accepts the receipt (a card transfer).

PaymentRow.description: One row of the payments screen.

kind.description: How the driver settles; null once the driver is no longer registered.

method.description: The method row's label ("کارت به کارت (ملت)") — a method payments were made with is never deleted.

summary.description: What the customer was told to pay to, as the driver words it (the masked card and its holder); null for a driver without one (the wallet).

reference.description: The gateway's own id of the payment (the wallet's ledger line); null when it has none (a card transfer).

receipt.description: The customer's receipt — always a picture: sent in the bot (it takes nothing else), or uploaded from the shop's website; null before it is sent. GET …/receipt serves either.

OrderSort.description: What the orders list sorts by: when each was placed (the list's own order), the amount.

sold.description: The orders of the list (its tab, type, search and days) that are sales: paid, being delivered or delivered.

SubscriptionRow.description: One row of the subscriptions screen: a client on a panel, as the shop last saw it there.

name.description: The client's name on the panel ("amir_2", "USER_7").

link.description: The one link the customer got.

plan.description: Null once the plan was deleted.

traffic.description: Bytes; a limit of 0 is no limit.

ip_limit.description: Devices at once; 0 is no limit.

duration_days.description: The term in days, counted from the first connection; 0 never expires.

auto_renew.description: The customer's «تمدید خودکار»: renewed from their wallet before the deadline.

next_period.description: A renewal queued behind the period in use (what that period leaves unused is not carried): when it begins, and the most it leaves then (bytes).

starts_at.description: When the first connection started the clock; null until then.

expires_at.description: Null while waiting for the first connection, or without a term.

expiring_soon.description: Active, its deadline within the expiring window (the list's `meta.expiring_days`).

last_synced_at.description: The moment the panel was last read for it — what the numbers are from.

actions.description: What the modal may do with it right now (the server's rules).

extend.description: Days and traffic on top: an active service that ends some day or has a quota.

SubscriptionExtensionRequest.description: What «افزایش زمان و حجم» gives one service on top of what it has — what a grant gives it —: at least one amount above zero, days only to a service that ends some day, traffic only to one with a quota. In an agent's shop the traffic comes out of the bot's (refused under `traffic_gb` when it is short); the days cost nothing.

days.description: Whole days, 0 to 365; blank is none.

note.description: Support's word to the customer, on its own line of the message; 300 characters at most.

notify.description: Whether the customer is told; they are unless it is false.

SubscriptionMoveRequest.description: A running service moved to another server with what is left of it. `leave_previous` moves it without asking its previous panel, out of reach — the old client stays there for the owner to remove (in an agent's shop only while that panel is out of reach).

SubscriptionDeleteRequest.description: A service deleted from its panel and the shop for good; the note goes to the customer when they hear at all (a service still active). `leave_panel` deletes it without asking its panel, out of reach — the client stays there (in an agent's shop only while that panel is out of reach).

SubscriptionSort.description: What the services list sorts by: when each was bought (the list's own order), when it ends — one that never does, or has not started, after every deadline —, the traffic used.

meta.description: `expiring`: active services ending within `expiring_days` (the tab's count; the dashboard's window too).

TicketStatus.description: Where a support ticket stands: open — waiting on support —, answered — support wrote last, waiting on the customer —, closed. A customer's message opens a ticket (again), support's answers it; either side closes it, support reopens it.

TicketAuthor.description: Who wrote a ticket's message: the customer, or support.

TicketChannel.description: Where a ticket's message was written: the shop's website or its bot (the customer's), a panel, the website's admin side (one of the shop's admins on it) or the report group (support's).

TicketAttachment.description: A message's picture — its bytes are the message's attachment address (…/messages/{message}/attachment).

name.description: Its name, as its sender's device gave it or one made up.

kept.description: Whether the shop keeps it still: a picture uploaded to a ticket goes 30 days after the ticket closed (one opened again keeps the pictures it still has; one already gone does not come back) — false then, the message saying it had one, its address a 404.

TicketRow.description: A support ticket, as the list shows it.

subscription.description: The customer's service it is about, by its name on the panel; null for none — or one deleted since.

last_message_at.description: When its latest message was written: the list's order.

rating.description: 1 to 5: the customer's word on it once it was closed; null for none.

closed_at.description: When it was closed; null while it is not — a ticket opened again leaves its end behind.

reviewer.description: Who of support wrote it: a panel's principal, a bot admin's @username, tg:<id> or user#<id> (in the report group or on the shop's website) — the owner's login reads «پشتیبانی» to anyone but the owner; null for the customer's.

TicketDetail.description: A support ticket with its whole conversation, the first message first.

subscription.description: The customer's service it is about, by its name on the panel; null for none — or one deleted since.

last_message_at.description: When its latest message was written: the list's order.

rating.description: 1 to 5: the customer's word on it once it was closed; null for none.

closed_at.description: When it was closed; null while it is not — a ticket opened again leaves its end behind.

rating_note.description: What the customer said with their rating.

open.description: The tickets waiting on an answer, whatever the list shows (the queue).

TicketMessageRequest.description: A ticket's message — support's answer on a panel, the customer's on their website —: its words. One with a picture comes as a form (TicketMessageUploadRequest).

body.description: 1 to 4000 characters, its line breaks kept.

TicketMessageUploadRequest.description: A ticket's message with its picture, as a browser form uploads it — a form without one is a message without a picture.

body.description: 1 to 4000 characters, its line breaks kept.

file.description: The picture: a JPEG, a PNG or a WebP, judged by its bytes — 10 MB at most; left out, none.

ReviewStatus.description: Where a customer's review stands: pending — waiting on support —, approved — the website shows it —, rejected — kept, never shown. Support moves it either way, at any time.

ReviewRow.description: A review written on the shop's website, as the moderation screen lists it — the writer's own words.

name.description: The name it is signed with.

body.description: Its words, line breaks as written.

context.description: A line of where they use the service from («ایرانسل · اندروید · Happ»); null for none.

customer.description: The customer who wrote it, signed in on the website; null for a guest's — or one whose account is gone.

reviewer.description: Who of support decided it last: a panel's principal, or one of the shop's admins on its website (@username, tg:<id> or user#<id>) — the owner's login reads «پشتیبانی» to anyone but the owner; null while it waits.

decided_at.description: When it was last approved or rejected; null while it waits.

actions.description: What its state allows support to decide (a delete, always).

pending.description: The reviews waiting on support, whatever the list shows (the queue).

ServerDriversResponse.description: The panel connectors a server is added with, in their order (each a PanelDriver): each one's words and the versions it needs (`notes`), what the add-server picker draws it by (`traits`: `mark`, two letters; `vendor`; `docs_url`) and what its panels can do (`inbounds`, `link_rotation`) — and a server's form on it: its name, the connector's connection, then the server's own columns.

form.description: Its form — the fields its connector's description (ServerDriversResponse) lists — as the server keeps it: how the shop signs in to the panel (`auth_mode`, and each secret as its SecretState: whether one is kept, never the secret), the connection's options, the server's own columns; null while this installation has not its connector.

serves_subscriptions.description: Whether the panel hands out subscription links as of the last check; null = never asked. A server without them cannot be sold.

unsellable_reason.description: Why nothing can be sold or moved onto the server now (switched off, without subscription links, full, its connector missing…); null when it can.

active_subscriptions.description: Its services running now, every shop's — the main bot's and the agents' bots': what its capacity counts.

shop_active_subscriptions.description: Of them, the shop's the panel has open — the ones its subscriptions screen lists (`?server=`); the rest are other shops'.

ProbeInbound.description: An inbound as the panel reports it — from a probe, or the cached copy in server_inbounds.

protocol.description: Null for what is not one protocol (a PasarGuard group).

port.description: Null for what has no port of its own (a PasarGuard group).

core_name.description: What the panel calls its core ("Xray"); null when it has no named one.

error.description: Persian sentence: what went wrong and what to change.

error_detail.description: Technical detail behind it (panel wording, cURL text), Latin.

inbounds.description: Null when the panel could not list them — a check then leaves the stored ones as they were.

serves_subscriptions.description: Whether the panel serves subscription links; null when that could not be asked.

subscription_probed.description: False when the connection worked but the subscription question failed.

ServerRequest.description: A server added or changed with its form, whole: its connector (`driver` — a saved server's own: a server's connector does not change) and the fields its description lists (ServerDriversResponse), by name, as typed — its name; the panel's address and the way in, an API token or an admin's username and password, one at a time (the other way's credentials are emptied); the connection's options; its own columns. A secret left blank or left out keeps the stored one while the panel's address stays on its host — moved to another, it is typed again —, and `clear_<name>: true` empties it. A closed shape per connector: tests/Unit/Drivers/DriverFormsTest holds each to its connector's form.

ServerGrantRow.description: «افزودن زمان و حجم»: a grant's part on a server — the grant's terms, and how far it got there, worked through a batch at a time.

mass_grant_id.description: The grant (a «هدیه همگانی») it is this server's part of, when it reaches beyond this server; null for a grant for this server alone.

agents_only.description: Only the agents' services (a mass gift for the agents).

reason.description: What the customers read with it.

notify.description: Whether the customers are told in the bot.

include_unstarted.description: The admin's tick: services still waiting for their first connection get it too, not only running ones.

total.description: Every active service it goes through, as issued — which of them takes it is the panel's word as each one's turn comes; granted + skipped + failed is how far it got.

skipped.description: Services it was not for when their turn came (switched off, gone, ended beyond what it gives, still waiting for their first connection without the tick).

waiting_reason.description: Why it waits at the service it was on, in the owner's words — what keeps the shop from working with the panel (ProviderErrorPresenter::describe(): out of reach, a credential refused or missing…); tried again by itself. Null while it moves on.

last_failure.description: The latest service the panel refused, and why.

ServerGrantsResponse.description: A server's grants card: its latest grants, and whom a new one would reach by what the shop last knew.

ServerGrantRequest.description: Days and traffic for the services on a server — an outage made good, a gift —: at least one amount above zero. It reaches the services running when it is issued, and those still waiting for their first connection only with `include_unstarted`; the reason goes to the customers, who hear it unless `notify` is false.

days.description: Whole days, 0 to 365; blank is none.

reason.description: Its own line of the message; 300 characters at most.

GrantReach.description: Whom a grant would reach by what the shop last knew: running services, and those still waiting for their first connection.

MassGrantAudience.description: Every service, the agents' only, or one server's.

MassGrantPart.description: A mass gift's part on one server: a server grant, worked through on its own.

MassGrantRow.description: A grant: days and traffic for the running services on every server (or the agents' only, or one server's — a server page's too), a part per server; its numbers are the parts' added up, its status and end its parts'.

server.description: The one server, for audience server.

MassGrantsResponse.description: The mass gift card: the latest grants — the servers' pages' too —, and whom a new one would reach — everyone, the agents, on each server.

MassGrantRequest.description: A server grant's terms (ServerGrantRequest) for every server at once — or the agents' services alone (what the bots of agents whose agency stands sold), or one server's.

days.description: Whole days, 0 to 365; blank is none.

reason.description: Its own line of the message; 300 characters at most.

server_id.description: For audience server, the server (a ServerRow.id); blank for the others.

BroadcastAudience.description: Whom it goes to: everyone, buyers, non-buyers, the inactive (no service running), a customer group, agents, one server's customers.

BroadcastRow.description: «ارسال همگانی»: a message a bot admin sent with /broadcast — copied or forwarded to an audience — or (kind unpin) the pins of one taken off again.

source_id.description: An unpin run: the broadcast whose pins it takes off.

mode.description: Copied from the bot (with the link buttons), or forwarded from its first sender.

id.description: The group or the server the audience names.

pin.description: Each message pinned in its chat.

pinned.description: Chats where its message is pinned still (what «لغو پین» would take off).

buttons.description: The admin's link buttons under a copy, rows in reading order.

content.description: What the message is: text, photo, video, animation, document, audio, voice, video_note, sticker, poll, other.

excerpt.description: Its text or caption, cut short.

total.description: Recipients when it started; sent + blocked + failed is how far it got.

admin.description: The bot admin who sent it; null for a run started from the panel.

reviewer.description: Who started it — from a panel or the shop's website: the agent's @bot, a bot admin's @username / tg:<id> / user#<id>, or the owner's login — «پشتیبانی» to anyone but the owner.

SecretState.description: A secret as the settings screen sees it: never the value, only whether one is stored and a recognisable hint.

url.description: APP_URL: the address the shop is reached at, its sub-folder included — every address the shop hands out is built on it.

MailTransport.description: How the shop's email goes out: none, or a mail driver's key (DriverDescription.key) — smtp, an account on a mail server; native, the host's own mail, as PHP's mail() sends it (php.ini's sendmail_path); resend, Resend's API (resend.com), with its API key and the sender's domain verified there.

MailEncryption.description: An SMTP connection: tls — STARTTLS, required; ssl — TLS from the first byte; none.

ConfigMailSettings.description: The shop's email (MAIL_* in config.php) — a website's sign-up codes and password resets, and the notices to a customer Telegram cannot reach, go out by it: how, every mail driver described with its settings, and who the emails come from.

from_address.description: The address the shop's emails come from; empty: no email goes out.

from_name.description: The name they come from; empty: the shop's name.

drivers.description: Every mail driver, its form described; its `sender` trait says which address its emails may come from.

values.description: Each driver's settings by its key — as config.php holds them, else their defaults; a secret as its SecretState.

ConfigSettingsResponse.description: The panel's own configuration, read from config.php.

timezones.description: Windows-style groups: one IANA id per zone, labelled "(UTC+03:30) وقت ایران".

cron_url.description: The cron trigger with its token masked, like the token; null without one. The whole address is GET /api/admin/settings/config/cron-url.

webhook_url.description: The main bot's webhook, its secret masked.

url.description: The cron trigger, token and all — for the screen's copy action; null without a token.

tables.description: How many tables its database holds

ConfigSettingsRequest.description: One group of the config.php settings, saved whole (PUT /settings/config/{group}) — the group's fields as ConfigSettingsResponse.groups names them. A secret left blank or left out keeps the stored one, `clear_<name>: true` empties it.

timezone.description: An IANA zone id (one of meta.timezones).

token.description: Left out or blank: the one kept stays — while the Bot API's address (`api_url`) stays on its host.

username.description: The bot's @username, the @ optional; blank for none.

api_url.description: The Bot API's address — http(s), a host, no credentials, ? or #. Moved to another origin (scheme, host or port), every bot's token goes there, agents' too: the save asks `current_password`.

current_password.description: The owner's current panel password, asked only while `api_url` moves to another origin (else not read): blank, or a wrong one — a failed sign-in, counted with the login's —, is a 422 on it and nothing is saved.

ConfigMailRequest.description: The shop's email, saved whole: the way out, and — for a mail driver — its settings by its form and who the emails come from. A closed shape per way out; what the other drivers keep stays as it is.

MailNoneRequest.description: No email at all: what the drivers keep stays, for a way back.

MailSmtpRequest.description: An account on a mail server, over SMTP.

port.description: 1 to 65535: 587 with tls, 465 with ssl, 25 without.

password.description: Left out or blank: the one kept stays — while the server, its port, the encryption and the username stay.

clear_password.description: True: the kept password is emptied.

from_address.description: An email address (kept in lower case).

from_name.description: 64 characters at most; blank: the shop's name.

MailNativeRequest.description: The host's own mail, as PHP's mail() sends it.

from_name.description: 64 characters at most; blank: the shop's name.

resend_key.description: Resend's API key, re_… as resend.com › API Keys shows it; left out or blank: the one kept stays — one is needed.

clear_resend_key.description: True: the kept key is emptied.

from_address.description: An email address (kept in lower case).

from_name.description: 64 characters at most; blank: the shop's name.

sent.description: True: the transport took it — whether it lands in the inbox is the mail server's.

log_level.description: One of meta.log_levels — any other is refused, as a time zone is.

TelegramTestRequest.description: A token to ask Telegram about; blank or left out — the stored one.

PlanServerRef.description: The server as the plan form and the plans table know it.

protocol.description: Null for what is not one protocol (a PasarGuard group).

port.description: Null for what has no port of its own (a PasarGuard group).

PlanServerEntry.description: One server a plan is sold on; `inbounds` is what a purchase gets today (resolved for whole-server entries).

unsellable_reason.description: Why customers are not offered this entry now (the server switched off, without subscription links, full, without a sellable inbound…); null when they are.

PlanCategoryRow.description: A group plans are filed under.

category.description: Null = uncategorised (sold under "سایر پلن‌ها" when the shop has categories).

sales.description: Its orders sold: paid, being delivered or delivered.

orders.description: Every order placed for it, whatever came of it; a plan that has any — or any service — is not deleted (switched off instead).

PlanOptions.description: The servers and inbounds the plan form can build entries from, and the categories.

price.description: Whole Toman; 0 for a free plan.

inbound_ids.description: The server's own enabled inbounds (PlanInboundRef.id); empty for the whole server.

name.description: Unique in the shop.

is_active.description: Absent: a new category starts on, a changed one keeps its switch.

expires_in.description: Seconds it waits for its token.

referral_code.description: An invite code the visitor came with: a newcomer becomes its owner's referral. Nothing for a customer the shop knows already.
