strong_sign_in.description: The website asks its admins a strong sign-in: Telegram, Google, or a password with its second step.

signed_in_strongly.description: This session was signed in so — or a strong way was proven on it since (POST /me/reauthenticate).

signed_in_until.description: Until when this session's sign-in lets it work the admin API at all — 12 hours after a way in was last proven on it; null: prove a way in again first (POST /me/reauthenticate).

recent_until.description: Until when this session's sign-in counts as recent — what a granted operation, and approving a payment (x-staff-recent), asks too; null: prove a way in again first (POST /me/reauthenticate).

StoreSession.description: A device the customer is signed in on.

device.description: What its browser said it is, in words: «Chrome در Windows».

ip.description: The address it signed in from.

last_used_at.description: Its last request — written every few minutes, not on each.

current.description: The one this request came with.

StoreTwoFactorResponse.description: The password was right for an account whose sign-in asks a second step: the challenge its code is posted with (POST /auth/login/2fa) — no session opened yet.

challenge.description: Posted back with the code; it takes five wrong codes.

expires_in.description: Seconds it waits for the code.

code.description: The six-digit code the account's authenticator app shows now (Persian digits and spaces too), or one of its recovery codes (dashes and spaces, any case).

StoreProfileRequest.description: The customer's names: a field sent is changed, one left out stays. A Telegram account's names are Telegram's.

last_name.description: 64 characters at most; blank for none.

current_password.description: The password now — required while the account has one.

password.description: The new one: 8 characters at least, 72 bytes at most (a Persian letter is two) — taken as typed.

StoreTwoFactorSetupResponse.description: A new secret for the customer's authenticator app, waiting for its first code.

secret.description: Base32 (160 bits): what the app takes when it is typed in by hand.

uri.description: The otpauth:// address the app takes it by — for a QR code, or a tap on the phone: the shop's name its issuer, the account's email its name.

code.description: The six digits the app shows now for the secret POST /me/2fa/setup gave (Persian digits too).

StoreRecoveryCodesResponse.description: Two-factor sign-in on: its recovery codes — each signs in once in place of the app's code —, shown this once (the shop keeps their keyed hashes only).

recovery_codes.description: Ten codes, each 10 capital letters and digits without look-alikes (no 0/O, 1/I/L).

StoreTelegramLinkRequest.description: A Telegram account proven as its sign-in proves one: the popup's id_token with the nonce it was opened with, or the redirect's code with its state.

nonce.description: The nonce POST /auth/nonce answered, which the popup was opened with.

code.description: What Telegram sent the browser back with.

state.description: The state it came back with: the one POST /me/telegram/authorize gave this customer (a sign-in's, or another customer's, proves nothing).

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier this browser made and kept when it began the sign-in — the one whose challenge it sent: another's opens nothing.

StoreGoogleLinkRequest.description: A Google account proven as its sign-in proves one: the id_token Google Identity Services handed the page, with the nonce it was asked for.

StoreEmailLinkRequest.description: An email for the account, and the password chosen to sign in by it. Every refusal at once, under its field.

email.description: An email address, 191 characters at most — kept in lower case.

password.description: 8 characters at least, 72 bytes at most — taken as typed.

code.description: Six digits (Persian digits too): what the email carried.

StoreIdentityKind.description: A kind of way in: a Telegram account, a Google account, an email (with its password).

StoreMergeOfferResponse.description: The way in being added is another account's of the shop: that account, for the customer to judge it is theirs too, which of the two stays, and the ticket that makes them one (POST /me/merge).

token.description: The merge ticket — this account's alone, once.

expires_in.description: Seconds it waits for the customer.

name.description: "first last"; null without one.

created_at.description: Since when it is the shop's customer.

telegram.description: A Telegram account signs it in.

google.description: A Google account signs it in.

keeps.description: The account that stays — the older: this one, or the other. Everything the other owns becomes its own; its ways in fill the empty slots.

token.description: The ticket the merge offer carried.

StoreReauthenticateRequest.description: A way into this account proven again: its password (and its second step's code while it asks one), its Telegram account — the popup's or the redirect's —, or its Google account.

code.description: While two-factor sign-in is on: the six-digit code the account's authenticator app shows now, or one of its recovery codes (spent) — as POST /auth/login/2fa takes it.

nonce.description: The nonce POST /auth/nonce answered, which the popup was opened with.

code.description: What Telegram sent the browser back with.

state.description: The state it came back with: the one POST /me/telegram/authorize gave this customer.

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier this browser made and kept when it began the sign-in — the one whose challenge it sent: another's opens nothing.

expires_in.description: Seconds this session may change how the account is signed in to before it is asked again (15 minutes).

StorePlan.description: A plan as the shop offers it now: what it gives and costs, the category it is filed under, the servers a customer may pick it on today.

duration_days.description: The term, counted from the first connection; 0 = it never ends.

category_id.description: The category it is offered under (its group's); null for the group of the rest — no category, or one switched off.

locations.description: The servers a customer may pick it on today («لوکیشن» in the bot), in the plan's order — at least one.

groups.description: Every active category in its order — an empty one too —, then, last, the plans of none (or of one switched off): without a category the shop has but this one group, or none when it sells nothing now.

category.description: Null for the group of the rest («سایر پلن‌ها» in the bot).

available.description: It takes a new customer now: switched on, serving subscription links, with room.

checked_at.description: When the shop last talked to it; null — never.

StoreSubscription.description: One of the customer's services, as the shop last saw it on its panel (`synced_at`), with what they may do with it now.

name.description: Its name on the panel ("amir_2", "USER_7").

plan.description: The plan it was sold or last renewed on; null once that plan was deleted.

server.description: The server it is on («لوکیشن» in the bot).

link.description: The one link the customer subscribes to; null once the panel no longer has the service (deleted).

auto_renew.description: «تمدید خودکار»: renewed from the wallet before its end, on its plan at its price.

offered.description: The switch may be set (PATCH): it runs, it ends some day, it has its plan, and the wallet is on.

days_before.description: How many days before its end it is renewed, its switch on — the shop's rule, one for every service (1 to 30).

renewable.description: Its customer may renew it now, on its plan: it is active or ended, its plan still there, renewing something — and in an agent's shop covered by their traffic.

link_rotation.description: Its link may be changed now (POST …/rotate-link): it runs, and its server can give it a new one.

next_period.description: Null while no renewal is queued behind the period in use.

presence.description: Whether it is connected — only when its panel was just asked (POST …/refresh) and has it; null otherwise.

online.description: Connected right now; null when the panel cannot tell.

last_online_at.description: Its last connection; null — never, or the panel cannot tell.

synced_at.description: When its panel was last read for it — what the numbers are from.

StoreServiceTraffic.description: A service's quota and what of it is used and left, in bytes.

StoreServiceTerm.description: A service's term: how long, when its clock started and when it ends — or that it waits for the first connection.

duration_days.description: The term in days, counted from the first connection; 0 = it never ends.

starts_at.description: When the first connection started the clock; null until then.

expires_at.description: Null while it waits for the first connection, or without a term.

awaits_first_use.description: Its term has not started: it starts at the first connection.

StoreNextPeriod.description: A renewal queued behind the period in use, what that period leaves unused not carried: when the period ends, and the most that is left then (bytes).

StorePayment.description: One attempt to pay an order.

receipt.description: The receipt the customer sent for it — in the bot, or from the website; null — none sent.

note.description: Support's word on its latest verdict — a rejection's reason, a cancellation's or a refund's note — as the bot tells the customer; null without one.

StoreOrder.description: An order of the customer's: what it was for, how far it got, its payments (the newest first).

plan.description: A purchase's or a renewal's plan; null for a wallet top-up, or once the plan was deleted.

server.description: Where a purchase was bought — a renewal's, where its service is; null for none.

subscription.description: The service it is about, by its name on the panel — a renewal's from the order's start, a purchase's once it is delivered — as a ticket names the service it is about; null for none, or once it was deleted.

StorePaymentMethod.description: A way to pay, as the checkout names it.

label.description: What its button says ("کارت به کارت (ملت)").

kind.description: instant — the wallet, paid at once; manual — a card transfer and its receipt; null for a way of paying no longer installed.

methods.description: In checkout order; none while the shop takes no way to pay that kind of order.

StoreOrderRequest.description: A purchase: the plan, the location it is bought on, and the way to pay it.

plan_id.description: A plan the shop sells now (GET /plans).

method_id.description: A way to pay a purchase (GET /payment-methods?for=purchase).

StoreRenewalRequest.description: A service's renewal: the way to pay it.

method_id.description: A way to pay a renewal (GET /payment-methods?for=renewal).

StoreTopUpRequest.description: A wallet top-up: how much, and the way to pay it.

amount.description: Toman, whole, as a customer types it — a JSON number or its text: Persian digits, thousands separators and «تومان» too — or as this API answers amounts (GET /wallet's "50000.00": a fraction of zero), within GET /wallet's `top_up` bounds.

method_id.description: A way to pay a top-up — any but the wallet itself (GET /payment-methods?for=wallet_topup).

StoreReceiptRequest.description: A card transfer's receipt, as a browser form uploads it.

file.description: The picture: a JPEG, a PNG or a WebP, judged by its bytes — 10 MB at most.

note.description: The customer's words with it, as support reads them — 1024 characters at most; blank for none.

StoreCheckout.description: What a checkout came to — a purchase, a renewal, a top-up. One that paid nothing is no answer but a refusal: the wallet short of the price (422 on `method_id`, what is missing), the order paid or closed elsewhere in the same moment (409).

outcome.description: settled — paid at once (the wallet): the order as it ended, `fulfilled` (a purchase's or a renewal's service in `subscription`) or `failed` (support finishes it, the money in: the order's own notes are support's, never shown) — and a request made again with its key whose order was paid since (by card too) and is done with: delivered, failed, or `refunded`; transfer — a card to transfer to (`transfer`), then the receipt (POST /payments/{id}/receipt): the payment awaits it, or has it with support; processing — paid, its delivery under way.

transfer.description: Where to transfer the money, and the payment the receipt is for — a transfer's; null for the rest.

payment_id.description: The payment its receipt is sent for.

card.description: The card's number, its 16 digits alone.

instructions.description: The shop's note on paying with it; null without one.

subscription.description: The service a purchase delivered or a renewal renewed, once delivered; null for the rest.

StoreRenewal.description: A service's renewal before it is paid: on its own plan, at that plan's price today, and the service as the renewal would leave it — by the shop's last copy of its panel's numbers (the renewal reads the panel as it is paid).

plan.description: The plan it is renewed on — its own: what a renewal on it gives.

after.description: The service as the renewal would leave it — as StoreSubscription has them: the days left always carry; the traffic a period leaves unused goes when it ends unless the shop carries it (`next_period`).

next_period.description: The period in use, its unused traffic going when it ends; null when nothing goes.

StoreWalletResponse.description: The customer's wallet. Amounts in Toman, as decimal strings.

credit.description: How far below zero an agent's wallet may go; '0.00' for anyone else.

spendable.description: What the wallet can pay now: the balance and the credit.

top_up.description: What a top-up may be, as the bot's «افزایش موجودی» offers it — POST /wallet/top-up takes these amounts as they are written here.

min.description: The smallest top-up the shop takes.

max.description: The largest top-up the shop takes.

presets.description: The amounts offered as buttons, ascending.

StoreWalletTransaction.description: One line of the customer's wallet ledger.

description.description: What it was for, in words («شارژ کیف پول (سفارش #12)»).

StoreReferralResponse.description: The customer's part in the referral program.

enabled.description: The program runs: a newcomer their code brings earns them a share of what that newcomer pays.

first_only.description: Only each newcomer's first payment earns it.

code.description: Their invite code — what a sign-in takes as `referral_code` (the site makes its own invite link with it).

bot_link.description: The bot's invite link with their code (https://t.me/<bot>?start=ref_<code>); null while the bot's @username is not known.

earned.description: What the commissions credited to them add up to, in Toman.

StoreNoticeType.description: What a notice was — one for each thing the shop's bot tells a customer on its own: a payment approved (the service delivered, the wallet charged — or the delivery failed and support finishes it), a receipt refused, an order cancelled by support, a payment back in the wallet, a wallet top-up given back, a payment reminder; a service switched off, back on, deleted, moved (its new link), given days or traffic; «یادآوری» — a service ending soon, its traffic running low; «تمدید خودکار» done, short of money, a renewal paid but not delivered; a newcomer their invite link brought, a referral's commission; their request to become an agent approved or rejected, their agency changed or ended, their bot's traffic short of an order; how their account is signed in to changed — two-factor sign-in turned off (by support, or by them) or on, a way in added or taken away, a password set, another account of theirs made one with it, its second step failed until it waits, the codes emailed to its address failed until none goes for a while (told on every door they have: Telegram and email both); support's answer to their ticket, and its closing.

StoreNotification.description: A notice the shop told the customer — the words its bot wrote them (the admin's, as Telegram got them, or would have).

text.description: Its words as plain text: no markup, line breaks as they are, a premium emoji its plain emoji.

html.description:
Its words as safe HTML — only b/strong, i/em, u/ins, s/strike/del, code, pre, blockquote, a spoiler as , a link to an http(s) address ( and no other attribute) and
for a line break; every text escaped. Safe to put in a page as it is.

subject.description: What it is about, for a link: one of their orders (GET /orders/{id} — a notice about a payment is about its order), of their services (GET /subscriptions/{id}) or of their tickets (GET /tickets/{id}); null for none — their account, a service deleted, someone else's row. Only a service may be gone since (a 404): support deleted it. An order stays — one nobody paid expires as `cancelled` —, and so does a ticket.

unread.description: How many of their notices they have not read, whatever the page shows.

StoreNotificationsReadRequest.description: The notices to mark read, by their numbers (at most 100); none sent (`{}`): every one.

unread.description: How many of their notices they have not read now.

StoreTicket.description: One of the customer's support tickets.

subscription.description: The service of theirs it is about, by its name; null for none — or one deleted since.

last_message_at.description: When its latest message was written: the list's order.

unread.description: Support wrote since they last read it (POST /tickets/{id}/read reads it, as the bot reads it once shown there).

rating.description: Their rating of it, 1 to 5, once it was closed; null for none — and once it opened again.

closed_at.description: When it was closed; null unless it is closed — a ticket opened again leaves its end behind.

StoreTicketMessage.description: One message of their ticket — theirs, or support's (who of support wrote it is never said: «پشتیبانی»).

body.description: Its words, line breaks as they are — plain text.

StoreTicketDetail.description: One of the customer's support tickets with its whole conversation, the first message first.

subscription.description: The service of theirs it is about, by its name; null for none — or one deleted since.

last_message_at.description: When its latest message was written: the list's order.

unread.description: Support wrote since they last read it (POST /tickets/{id}/read reads it, as the bot reads it once shown there).

rating.description: Their rating of it, 1 to 5, once it was closed; null for none — and once it opened again.

closed_at.description: When it was closed; null unless it is closed — a ticket opened again leaves its end behind.

rating_note.description: What they said with their rating.

unread.description: How many of all of their tickets hold support's words they have not read, whatever the list shows (a badge).

StoreTicketRequest.description: A ticket opened: what it is about, its first message, and the service of theirs it is about. One with a picture comes as a form (StoreTicketUploadRequest).

body.description: 1 to 4000 characters, its line breaks kept.

subscription_id.description: One of their services (GET /subscriptions); left out, null or blank — about none.

StoreTicketUploadRequest.description: A ticket opened with a picture in its first message, as a browser form uploads it — a form without one opens it without a picture.

body.description: 1 to 4000 characters, its line breaks kept.

subscription_id.description: One of their services (GET /subscriptions); left out, null or blank — about none.

file.description: The picture: a JPEG, a PNG or a WebP, judged by its bytes — 10 MB at most; left out, none.

StoreTicketRatingRequest.description: Their rating of a closed ticket — a rating given before is replaced.

note.description: What they say with it — 500 characters at most; blank for none.

StoreReview.description: A review the shop shows: approved by support. Its writer's own words and choices — plain text, which the website escapes —, nothing of who wrote it nor of support's.

name.description: The name it is signed with.

body.description: Its words, line breaks as written.

context.description: A line of where they use the service from («ایرانسل · اندروید · Happ»); null for none.

avatar.description: The key of the website's own avatar they picked; null for none — the website draws its own default.

summary.description: Every review the shop shows, as one figure — whatever page this is.

average.description: Their mean rating, to two decimals; null while there is none.

StoreReviewRequest.description: A review written on the website. Every refusal at once, under its field.

name.description: 2 to 64 characters, on one line: the name it is signed with, shown with it.

body.description: 10 to 600 characters, its line breaks kept.

context.description: A line of where they use the service from — «ایرانسل · اندروید · Happ» —, 100 characters at most; blank for none.

avatar.description: The key of one of the website's own avatars — 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, - and _, never an address —; blank for none.

captcha.description: The captcha widget's token, while the website asks one (GET / says which, and how to draw it), solved for the operation's action (its `x-captcha`).

status.description: pending: waiting on support until it is approved.
